messages:
eli: Heads-up: Kaida cutover dry-run showed intermittent audit bundles arriving and some dropped envelopes. Cutover is scheduled TOMORROW 09:30 PT. Can infra + sec look? @meera @cal :mag:

meera: Which bundles are missing? VPC flow, CloudTrail, or both? Any errors from the forwarder/ingest?

cal: Quick triage: a few things at once. 1) Our forwarder successfully PUTs to their S3 but some objects are 0-bytes on the Splunk side due to the customer's proxy terminating TLS with our SNI mismatch. 2) Separately, when we attempted a cross-account replay using their managed key we hit kms:GenerateDataKey -> AccessDenied for a subset of test objects. CloudTrail shows both failures.

eli: Ugh—network + KMS. Both create compliance/renewal risk if logs >24h missing. What's the short mitigation?

cal: Network: their corporate proxy only permits outbound hosts with a CN that matches their org-owned cert SAN list. Our forwarder uses a generic redwood.example.com certificate chain, so the proxy drops the connection mid-stream resulting in truncated uploads. Workaround: 1) We can switch the forwarder to use the customer's custom SNI (if they provide a TLS cert that we can host behind a dedicated endpoint) OR 2) route via a Redwood-managed egress IP that they've whitelisted. Network team estimate: 2-4h for customer cert onboarding, 30-60m for egress IP route if they already whitelist.

meera: KMS: their key policy uses a restrictive "aws:PrincipalOrgID" condition that excludes cross-account roles. Proposed minimal change: add a single statement allowing our forwarder role for kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Encrypt scoped to the key ARN and condition on aws:SourceAccount + aws:SourceArn. We must include CSR tag and schedule an automatic revert in 2h. I'll draft the snippet.

cal: Please also confirm we won't break their org guardrails. If the customer refuses a policy change, fallback is Redwood-managed key for the forwarder path (short-lived) combined with the egress-IP whitelist to avoid proxy issues. That path preserves their key guardrails but needs customer agreement for transient managed-key.

meera: Draft minimal KMS statement (will tighten to exact key ARN before prod):

```
{
  "Sid": "AllowKaidaForwarder",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDWOOD_ACCOUNT:role/log-forwarder"},
  "Action": ["kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:Encrypt"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:999900001111:key/kaida-abc",
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:SourceAccount": "999900001111","aws:SourceArn": "arn:aws:s3:::kaida-logs-*"}}
}
```

meera: I'll run staging with that and tag CSR-KAIDA-42. ETA for staging test: ~45m.

ops-bot: Job queued: forwarder-staging -> kaida (job 22334). ETA 20m.

eli: For CS messaging, keep it focused: root cause, two mitigations (managed-key fallback + egress-IP), ETA for staging validation, and explicit ask: does Kaida want us to request their network team to whitelist Redwood egress IPs? Also mark renewal watch.

cal: Network note: If we go the egress-IP route we need their firewall PO and expected time for whitelist. That often takes 1 business day unless they pre-approve. So ask them now. The customer's compliance manager is on the onboarding thread.

meera: Staging results: KMS staging test PASSed (GenerateDataKey + PutObject successful). Pushed CSR-KAIDA-42 with audit tag and scheduled revert. Pasting test logs output: "PutObject OK, GenerateDataKey OK, CloudTrail entries show success."

ops-bot: Deployment succeeded: forwarder-staging (job 22334).

cal: Network still needs action. I recommend we 1) offer the egress-IP whitelist as the fastest customer-visible mitigation (if they can whitelist quickly) and 2) pursue customer cert onboarding in parallel for long-term stability.

eli: Meera—once you have prod signoff from security post-CSR, push prod patch during the maintenance window. Cal—prepare the egress-IP whitelist packet to send to the customer's network team (include IPs, ports, SNI guidance).

meera: Security approved the scoped KMS exception for prod (CSR-KAIDA-42) with exact key ARN and principal. Revert scheduled after 2h unless customer requests a permanent entry. Proceed during the 2-hour maintenance window.

eli: CS draft for CSMs (please personalize): "Quick update: During pre-cutover validation we found two causes for missing audit bundles: (1) your network proxy is terminating connections due to SNI/cert constraints, causing truncated uploads; (2) a KMS key policy prevented Redwood's forwarder from encrypting some log objects. We've validated a scoped KMS fix in staging and are ready to roll to prod during the maintenance window. Short-term options: we can provide a Redwood-managed key temporarily and/or request your network team whitelist a Redwood egress IP to bypass the proxy. Please let us know which you prefer; if you can start the firewall whitelist now it will speed coverage. We'll update within 3 hours."

cal: I'll assemble the egress packet now. eli: please flag renewal-watch for AMs (if >24h retention gap escalate).

eli: Owner: meera (KMS), cal (network). Status: blocker: resolved-in-staging (KMS), network: action-required (awaiting customer whitelist or cert). Next: prod-roll for KMS (ETA 90m) and network follow-up. :white_check_mark:
